The latter construction enforces convexity directly, rather than full dual feasibility. We implement it using multiplier estimates from the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). On 431 instances from six problem families, the complete method certifies 296 optima, compared with 156 for the conic-bundle method MIQCR-CB and 187 for direct Gurobi under a common time budget.
tldr: The paper develops MIQCR-FR, a framework for exact convex reformulations of equality-constrained binary quadratic programs using facially reduced semidefinite relaxations and dual multiplier recovery.
motivation: Standard mixed-integer quadratic convex reformulation (MIQCR) relies on dual multipliers from the original semidefinite relaxation, but facial reduction reduces the semidefinite matrix order and generally does not guarantee recovery of those original dual multipliers.
method: The authors retain linear equalities and their products with each binary variable to enable dual recovery, give a dual recovery formula for extending reduced-dual feasible solutions, provide a spectral shift for approximate multipliers, and formulate either a trust-region subproblem or a reduced eigenvalue calculation, implementing the latter with ADMM.
result: On 431 instances from six problem families, the complete method certifies 296 optima, compared with 156 for the conic-bundle method MIQCR-CB and 187 for direct Gurobi under a common time budget.
conclusion: The proposed MIQCR-FR framework yields exact convex reformulations and substantially improves computational certification for equality-constrained binary quadratic programs.

title: The Invariant Subspace Problem And Rosenblum Operators Ii
authors: Junsheng Fang, Bingzhe Hou, Chunlan Jiang, Yuanhang Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the separable, infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. In the first paper of this series, we introduced, by means of the Rosenblum operators, the shift representation operators [MATH], which relate an operator [MATH] with [MATH] to the unilateral shift [MATH] and reveal its hidden analytic structure. In this paper we replace the pair [MATH] by the Sobolev disk algebra [MATH] and the multiplication operator [MATH], whose canonical left inverse [MATH] plays the role of [MATH], and study the two-parameter family [MATH]. We prove that [MATH] with [MATH] is intransitive whenever there exist a nonzero vector [MATH] and a nontrivial [MATH]-invariant manifold [MATH] such that [MATH] has a zero in the closed unit disk for every [MATH]; the proof explicitly constructs a nontrivial invariant subspace of [MATH]. We further introduce the ideal property and show that every intransitive operator on [MATH] is unitarily equivalent to an operator on [MATH] with this property, so that the Invariant Subspace Problem for arbitrary operators reduces to a problem about a concrete function algebra. Applications include a characterization of intransitivity through the rationality of the generating function [MATH] and new results on Pearcy's problem. Our main application is Halmos's third problem, which has remained open for more than fifty years: we reduce it to invertible operators with conjugate bi-geometric form, and we prove that [MATH] is intransitive for every invertible [MATH] admitting a nontrivial projection [MATH] with [MATH] and [MATH] of rank one. Finally, we exhibit tridiagonal operators that are intransitive and admit infinite decreasing chains of invariant subspaces.
tldr: This paper studies the invariant subspace problem using Rosenblum operators and the Sobolev disk algebra, proving intransitivity conditions and reducing Halmos's third problem to a concrete class of operators.
motivation: The invariant subspace problem and Halmos's third problem are long-standing open questions in operator theory on Hilbert spaces.
method: The authors introduce a two-parameter family of shift representation operators associated with the Sobolev disk algebra, construct nontrivial invariant subspaces, and establish an ideal property for intransitive operators.
result: They prove intransitivity for operators satisfying certain zero conditions, characterize intransitivity via rationality of a generating function, and show that every invertible operator with a rank-one projection satisfying specific conditions is intransitive, thereby reducing Halmos's third problem.
conclusion: The work advances pure operator theory but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Weighted Schatten P-numerical Radii Via Generalized Aluthge Transformation
authors: Sumit Chandok Kallal Pal
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we derive various weighted p-numerical radius inequalities using the Schatten p-norm with the generalized Aluthge transform for operators in Hilbert spaces. In addition, the article explores classical numerical radius and norm inequalities for operators. The bounds obtained in this work improve upon several well-known previous results. In addition, we provide examples where we calculate and analyze upper bounds for the weighted numerical radius of different types of matrices using generalized Aluthge transformation.
tldr: This paper derives weighted Schatten p-numerical radius inequalities for Hilbert space operators using the generalized Aluthge transform.
motivation: The authors aim to improve existing numerical radius and norm inequalities by introducing weighted versions through Schatten p-norms and generalized Aluthge transformations.
method: They establish bounds for the weighted p-numerical radius via the generalized Aluthge transform and compare these with classical numerical radius inequalities, illustrating with matrix examples.
result: The derived bounds improve several well-known previous inequalities, and explicit upper bounds are calculated for various matrix classes.
conclusion: The work is a contribution to operator theory and matrix analysis, offering refined inequalities for weighted numerical radii, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: PyCache Trap: The Inspection-Execution Gap In Agent Skill Scanners
authors: Jie Liao, Simeng Qin, Wenqi Ren, Wei Zhou, Junhao Wen, Ranjie Duan, Yang Liu, Xiaojun Jia
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills combine instructions with executable resources, giving third-party packages access to an agent's runtime. Existing skill scanners inspect documentation and visible source, but Python may execute a bundled bytecode cache with different behavior. We study this gap between inspection and execution through PyCache Trap, which pairs benign source with a substituted cache accepted by the loader and connects it to a task-relevant invocation. Scanner-guided rewriting changes the invocation wording while preserving the cache body, separating package admission from recognition of the concealed behavior. Across 100 skills and seven scanners, PyCache Trap achieves 94-100% attack success, with no semantic recognition of the cache-resident behavior. We propose execution-aware validation (EAV) to connect inspected instructions, scripts, imports, and runtime artifacts in a typed execution graph. EAV combines grounded behavioral analysis with trusted reproduction of compiled artifacts. It detects all 100 evaluated source-present cache substitutions and reaches 92.8% Recall at 10.0% FPR across five attack families and 200 benign skills. The results support checking the executable artifacts a runtime can select as part of skill admission, within the supported loaders and code-object normalization. The code is released at [URL].
tldr: The paper identifies and exploits an inspection-execution gap in agent skill scanners via Python bytecode cache substitution, then proposes execution-aware validation to detect such attacks.
motivation: Agent skills can bundle executable resources, and existing scanners inspect only documentation and visible source while Python may load a substituted bytecode cache with different behavior.
method: The authors construct PyCache Trap, which pairs benign source with a malicious cache accepted by the loader and task-relevant invocation, and evaluate it against 100 skills and seven scanners; they also propose execution-aware validation (EAV) using a typed execution graph and trusted reproduction.
result: PyCache Trap achieves 94-100% attack success with no semantic recognition of hidden behavior, while EAV detects all 100 evaluated cache substitutions and reaches 92.8% recall at 10.0% false positive rate.
conclusion: The findings show that skill admission should check executable artifacts a runtime can select, and EAV offers a detection approach within supported loaders and code-object normalization.

title: Power Side-Channel Membership Inference Attack On Embedded Machine Learning
authors: Prabhat Mishra Sahan Sanjaya
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) threaten the privacy of machine learning (ML) training data by determining whether a sample was used to train a target model. Existing MIAs rely on model outputs, ranging from prediction probabilities to predicted labels, an assumption that can be restrictive for on-device ML systems with limited or inaccessible outputs. However, suppressing model outputs does not eliminate the data-dependent computations that produce them, which may remain observable through physical side channels. We present PSCMIA, a power side-channel membership inference attack against embedded ML models that can infer membership directly from power traces without requiring prediction probabilities or even the predicted labels. We evaluate PSCMIA across multiple datasets (MNIST, FMNIST, CIFAR10, CINIC10), fully connected (FC) and convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, and two embedded platforms (STM32F3, XMEGA). PSCMIA achieves ROC-AUC values of up to 0.907 on FC models. For CNN models, the ROC-AUC gap between PSCMIA and probability vector-based shadow MIA ranges from 0.006 to 0.116. Across the FC and CNN evaluations, PSCMIA outperforms label-only MIA in 11 of 16 model-dataset-hardware configurations, demonstrating that physical execution can expose membership information even when conventional model outputs are unavailable through unintended power side-channel leakage.
tldr: The paper presents PSCMIA, a power side-channel membership inference attack that infers whether data was used to train an embedded machine learning model directly from power traces without relying on model outputs.
motivation: Existing membership inference attacks typically require access to model outputs such as prediction probabilities or labels, which may be unavailable in on-device ML systems; however, the underlying computations can still leak information through physical side channels.
method: The authors collect power traces from embedded platforms and use side-channel analysis to infer training membership, evaluating fully connected and convolutional neural networks on MNIST, FMNIST, CIFAR10, and CINIC10 across STM32F3 and XMEGA hardware.
result: PSCMIA achieves ROC-AUC up to 0.907 on fully connected models, is competitive with probability-vector shadow MIAs on CNNs with AUC gaps of 0.006 to 0.116, and outperforms label-only MIA in 11 of 16 configurations.
conclusion: Physical execution can expose membership information through unintended power side-channel leakage even when conventional model outputs are suppressed, highlighting a privacy threat for embedded machine learning.

title: Near-Inverse-Linear Barriers For Explicit Affine Witness Isolation
authors: Sebastian Ben Daniel
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study randomized nonuniform polynomial-size transformations that output explicit binary affine filters for circuit inputs whose nonempty satisfying sets are affine. The filter may depend on the entire input description; no affine basis is supplied. For every fixed [MATH], a worst-case singleton success guarantee [MATH], where [MATH] is the witness arity, implies [MATH]. More generally, any success guarantee [MATH] yields satisfiability circuits of size [MATH] for length-[MATH] descriptions with at most [MATH] witness variables, hence subexponential in [MATH] when [MATH]. Conversely, SAT search-to-decision gives deterministic perfect isolation, making polynomial-resource fixed-exponent strong affine isolation equivalent to [MATH]. For explicit unions of at most [MATH] affine components, success [MATH] implies the same collapse whenever [MATH] and [MATH]. The inverse-linear endpoint is not claimed.
tldr: The paper studies randomized nonuniform polynomial-size transformations that output explicit binary affine filters for affine satisfying sets, deriving near-inverse-linear barriers and collapse consequences for satisfiability circuits.
motivation: To understand the limitations of explicit affine witness isolation and its connections to SAT search-to-decision and circuit complexity.
method: Analyzes randomized nonuniform polynomial-size transformations with worst-case singleton success guarantees, using affine filters without a supplied affine basis.
result: Any success guarantee yields satisfiability circuits of size subexponential in the number of witness variables when certain parameter conditions hold, and strong affine isolation is equivalent to a collapse; analogous results hold for explicit unions of affine components.
conclusion: The inverse-linear endpoint is not claimed, but the work establishes barriers and equivalences for explicit affine witness isolation within classical computational complexity.

title: A Survey Of Security Research For Operating Systems
authors: Masaki Hashimoto, Ruo Ando, Toshiyuki Maeda, Hidehiko Tanaka
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, information systems have become the social infrastructure, so that their security must be improved urgently. In this paper, we introduce the results of the survey of virtualization, operating system verification and access control technologies in association with the design requirements of the reference monitor. Additionally, we show the prospects and challenges for each technology.
tldr: A survey of operating system security research covering virtualization, OS verification, and access control technologies organized around reference monitor design requirements.
motivation: Information systems have become critical social infrastructure, making their security an urgent concern that motivates a systematic review of foundational OS-level security mechanisms.
method: Literature survey and comparative analysis of virtualization, operating system verification, and access control techniques, framed in relation to reference monitor design requirements.
result: The paper consolidates existing results across these three technology areas and identifies prospects and open challenges for each.
conclusion: The survey provides a roadmap of OS security technologies while highlighting remaining gaps and future research directions for building trustworthy systems.

title: Eifl: Efficiently Protecting Global Model Privacy And Integrity Against An Untrusted Server In Federated Learning
authors: Zehui Liao, Qiang Li, Binghui Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) typically adopts a server-client architecture, where the server aggregates clients' local models (i.e., the input) and returns the aggregated global model (i.e., the output) to clients. An untrusted server may return a tampered global model to compromise the output integrity. Some existing schemes focus on verifying the output integrity. However, these schemes mostly rely on clients pre-negotiating a set of identical auxiliary information among themselves and keeping it confidential from the server. This dependency creates a verification vulnerability: if the auxiliary information is leaked, the verification method may be circumvented. Additionally, in some privacy-sensitive scenarios (e.g., commercial federated learning), the global model may need to be kept confidential from an untrusted server. However, only a few works achieve the output privacy while addressing verification vulnerability, at the cost of prohibitive computation and communication overhead. To address these challenges simultaneously, we propose a novel provably privacy-preserving FL method called EIFL. Specifically, we adopt a two-stage aggregation and combine it with symmetric encryption to protect the output privacy. To address the verification vulnerability, we propose an efficient verification method based on vector inner product for output integrity, and a random vector generation method for clients to agree on auxiliary information. EIFL innovatively binds the auxiliary information to the output integrity, and eliminates the need to keep the auxiliary information confidential from the server. Moreover, EIFL is robust against client dropout during the verification phase through a simple resending operation. Evaluation results validate the advantages of EIFL over state-of-the-art schemes in terms of computation and communication overhead.
tldr: EIFL is a federated learning scheme that protects global model privacy and verifies output integrity against an untrusted server using two-stage aggregation, symmetric encryption, and vector inner-product verification.
motivation: Existing federated learning verification schemes rely on clients pre-negotiating and keeping confidential auxiliary information, creating a vulnerability if leaked, while privacy-preserving alternatives incur prohibitive overhead.
method: The authors combine two-stage aggregation with symmetric encryption for output privacy, and propose an inner-product-based verification method plus a random vector generation scheme that binds auxiliary information to output integrity without requiring confidentiality from the server.
result: EIFL achieves provable privacy preservation and integrity verification while remaining robust to client dropout via simple resending, and evaluations show lower computation and communication overhead than state-of-the-art schemes.
conclusion: The work addresses classical federated learning security and efficiency, with no connection to quantum information theory, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fourier Quasicrystals With Positive Integer Masses Are Sections Of Lee-Yang Cycles
authors: Dongsheng Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize Fourier quasicrystal measures with positive integer masses as real sections of effective Lee-Yang cycles, with weighted local intersection degrees. The section matrix has positive maximal minors, and the mass at each root is its weighted local intersection degree. For Delone support the reduced support of the cycle can be chosen strict. The support of every integer-mass Fourier quasicrystal measure is the common complex zero set of finitely many real-valued trigonometric polynomials. For unit masses the representing cycle can be chosen reduced, with local degree one at every physical root. These results answer Questions (1), (2), and (4) of Alon, Kummer, Kurasov, and Vinzant. The proof recovers a finite-dimensional torus from the spectrum, proves that the resulting analytic set is algebraic, and reconstructs its complex branches and their integer coefficients from their moments. A support-height theorem for holonomic sequences gives the required linear spectral bound. Singular Lee-Yang sections are Fourier quasicrystal measures with their natural local intersection degrees; discarding those degrees can destroy the Fourier quasicrystal property.
tldr: The paper characterizes Fourier quasicrystal measures with positive integer masses as real sections of effective Lee-Yang cycles, answering several open questions in harmonic analysis and algebraic geometry.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the structure of Fourier quasicrystal measures, which are measures with discrete support whose Fourier transform is also discrete, by connecting them to Lee-Yang cycles and local intersection theory.
method: They use weighted local intersection degrees of Lee-Yang cycles, a support-height theorem for holonomic sequences, and reconstruct complex branches and integer coefficients from moments to prove that the resulting analytic set is algebraic and recover a finite-dimensional torus from the spectrum.
result: They show that every integer-mass Fourier quasicrystal measure's support is the common complex zero set of finitely many real-valued trigonometric polynomials, and for unit masses the representing cycle can be chosen reduced with local degree one at every physical root.
conclusion: The work resolves Questions (1), (2), and (4) of Alon, Kummer, Kurasov, and Vinzant, and demonstrates that singular Lee-Yang sections are Fourier quasicrystal measures whose natural local intersection degrees cannot be discarded without losing the Fourier quasicrystal property.

title: Optimal Diffractive Focusing Of Vortex Beams
authors: Roohollah Ghobadi, Carrie Rodriguez, Lukas Scarfe, Maxim A. Efremov, Ebrahim Karimi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate diffractive ring focusing of paraxial beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) through a finite circular aperture as a variational optimization problem. For a fixed topological charge, we determine the real-valued radial pupil that maximizes the intensity at a prescribed ring radius and propagation distance under a normalization constraint on the input field. The resulting problem admits an exact analytical solution: the optimal pupil combines the familiar Fresnel phase structure with an OAM-dependent Bessel radial modulation, and the associated eigenvalue yields a rigorous upper bound on the achievable ring intensity. We further analyze the lens-assisted configuration and derive a simple bound that allows direct comparison between diffractive and refractive vortex focusing. The theory also provides a quantitative framework for evaluating the performance of practical mask designs, including binary Fresnel-Bessel zone plates and amplitude-weighted pupils. We have experimentally tested our predictions in the optical domain by implementing the corresponding vortex beam pupils and comparing their propagation and focusing performance with the optimal solution. Our results establish the vortex-beam analogue of optimal amplitude-only focusing and identify the fundamental limits governing diffractive concentration of structured waves.
tldr: The paper formulates and experimentally demonstrates optimal diffractive focusing of paraxial vortex beams carrying orbital angular momentum using a variational approach that yields an OAM-dependent Bessel-modulated pupil.
motivation: Vortex beams with orbital angular momentum are widely used in structured light applications, but fundamental limits on their diffractive focusing through finite apertures were not fully characterized.
method: The authors cast diffractive ring focusing through a circular aperture as a variational optimization problem, solve for the optimal real-valued radial pupil analytically, and test the predictions with optical experiments.
result: The optimal pupil combines Fresnel phase structure with an OAM-dependent Bessel radial modulation, yielding a rigorous upper bound on ring intensity and providing a framework to compare diffractive and refractive vortex focusing.
conclusion: These results establish the vortex-beam analogue of optimal amplitude-only focusing and identify fundamental limits for diffractive concentration of structured waves.

title: Topological Spatiotemporal Mode-Locked Lasers
authors: Xiaokang Lian, Yuchen Zhang, Mutian Xu, Bing Han, Chengkun Cai, Jun Liu, Jian Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving robust high-dimensional solitons both in optics and Bose-Einstein condensates remains a great challenge, due to unpredictable high-order perturbations. Here we propose and demonstrate a novel topological spatiotemporal mode-locked fiber laser empowered by mode-division multiplexing, for precisely controlling of the spatiotemporal solitons. By introducing time delays between the individual transverse mode paths, a topological spatiotemporal lattice is formed in the multimode cavity, which in turn excites periodic spatiotemporal solitons. These solitons are stable against the perturbations, attributed to periodic potentials induced by the nonreciprocal dissipative coupling interactions. Moreover, under the thermodynamic limit, the solitons condense into nested-type spatiotemporal solitons, a phenomenon analogous to the Bose-Einstein condensate of matter waves. Our results indicate that topological spatiotemporal mode-locked lasers not only constitute a controllable source of robust spatiotemporal light bullets, but also provide a valuable platform for exploring nonlinear high-dimensional soliton dynamics and non-Hermitian topological physics.
tldr: The paper proposes and demonstrates a topological spatiotemporal mode-locked fiber laser using mode-division multiplexing to generate stable high-dimensional solitons.
motivation: Robust high-dimensional solitons are difficult to realize due to unpredictable high-order perturbations, motivating a topological approach for precise control.
method: Time delays between individual transverse mode paths in a multimode cavity form a topological spatiotemporal lattice, enabling periodic spatiotemporal solitons stabilized by nonreciprocal dissipative coupling.
result: The solitons are stable against perturbations and, in the thermodynamic limit, condense into nested-type spatiotemporal solitons analogous to a Bose-Einstein condensate.
conclusion: Topological spatiotemporal mode-locked lasers provide a controllable source of robust light bullets and a platform for nonlinear soliton dynamics and non-Hermitian topological physics.

title: Performance Analysis And Sensing-Aware Resource Allocation For Full-Duplex Massive Mimo Iscc Networks
authors: Vo Phi Son, Van-Dinh Nguyen, Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Tuan-Vu Truong, Symeon Shatzinotas
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emerging edge applications must sense their environment and process data within tight latency budgets. Full-duplex (FD) integrated sensing, communication, and computing (ISCC) supports these functions concurrently, but radar probing interferes with uplink reception while user transmissions degrade target estimation. These coupled effects call for joint sensing and offloading decisions. We investigate a FD massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) ISCC network in which users partially offload tasks to an edge server while an access point probes a target. For zero-forcing uplink reception with imperfect channel estimates, we derive a tractable rate bound and target-angle Cramer-Rao lower bounds (CRLBs) under the stated interference and beam-alignment assumptions. We then jointly optimize offloading fractions, user and radar transmit powers, and edge computing resources to minimize average end-to-end task latency subject to sensing-accuracy, communication-rate, energy, deadline, and resource constraints. A successive convex approximation algorithm is developed to efficiently address the resulting nonconvex problem. The analysis shows that larger arrays improve sensing and uplink performance, but residual radar interference creates a finite rate ceiling when user powers scale down with array size. Simulation results show joint allocation reduces radar transmit power by approximately 86% relative to equal communication-user power at a -40 dB CRLB threshold and lowers latency compared with fixed-allocation and half-duplex schemes.
tldr: This paper analyzes a full-duplex massive MIMO integrated sensing, communication, and computing (ISCC) network and jointly optimizes offloading, transmit powers, and edge computing resources to minimize end-to-end task latency under sensing-accuracy and communication constraints.
motivation: Emerging edge applications need to sense their environment and process data within tight latency budgets, but in full-duplex ISCC systems radar probing interferes with uplink reception while user transmissions degrade target estimation, creating coupled tradeoffs that require joint design.
method: The authors derive a tractable uplink rate bound for zero-forcing reception with imperfect channel estimates and Cramér-Rao lower bounds for target-angle estimation, then formulate a nonconvex latency-minimization problem and solve it via successive convex approximation.
result: Larger antenna arrays improve both sensing and uplink performance, but residual radar interference imposes a finite rate ceiling; joint allocation reduces radar transmit power by roughly 86% relative to equal communication-user power at a -40 dB CRLB threshold and lowers latency versus fixed-allocation and half-duplex schemes.
conclusion: Joint sensing-aware resource allocation is essential for efficient full-duplex massive MIMO ISCC networks, though the work remains a classical wireless-communications engineering contribution.

title: How Many Directions Must A Truncated Diffusion Sampler Retain? Matching Bounds Under Power-Law Spectra
authors: Radmehr Karimian, Ali Mohades, Johannes Lederer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion samplers can reduce computation by generating selected spectral coordinates and filling the remaining directions with noise. How many directions must they retain? We study this question for data with power-law covariance spectra. For Gaussian data compared to a smoothed target, we prove matching bounds on the required number of retained directions, provided that the ambient dimension is sufficiently large. The truncation error depends on the combined Wiener gains of the omitted directions, regardless of the accuracy of the sampler on the retained coordinates. Keeping only directions whose signal exceeds the output noise level can therefore leave a non-vanishing error: many individually weak directions remain significant in aggregate. Combining this characterization with a diffusion convergence bound yields sufficient sampling-step complexity under exact scores. The upper bounds also extend to estimated principal components and, componentwise, to Gaussian mixtures. The practical prescription is to select the retained subspace using an aggregate spectral-tail error budget, then to choose the diffusion noise level accordingly.
tldr: The paper proves matching bounds on how many spectral directions a truncated diffusion sampler must retain under power-law covariance spectra.
motivation: Diffusion samplers can save computation by generating only selected spectral coordinates and filling the rest with noise, but it is unclear how many directions must be kept to control error.
method: For Gaussian data and a smoothed target, it proves matching bounds on the required number of retained directions when the ambient dimension is large, then combines the truncation characterization with a diffusion convergence bound to obtain sampling-step complexity.
result: The truncation error depends on the combined Wiener gains of omitted directions, so retaining only directions above the output noise level can leave non-vanishing error because many individually weak directions matter in aggregate.
conclusion: The practical prescription is to select the retained subspace using an aggregate spectral-tail error budget and then choose the diffusion noise level accordingly.

title: Continuous Policy And Value Iteration For Stochastic Control Problems With Inhomogeneous Synchronous Coupling
authors: Qi Feng, Renjie Shao, Gu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a continuous policy-value iteration framework for infinite horizon stochastic control problems, in which the policy evolves through Langevin type dynamics driven by the gradient of the inhomogeneous Hamiltonian, while the value function is updated simultaneously with optimal policy iterations, avoiding directly solving its corresponding PDE at each iteration. The iteration scheme enjoys policy improvement under suitable regularity and admissibility assumptions. We show the exponential contraction of the joint policy value dynamics in Wasserstein-2 distance under the Lipschitz condition in expectation via the inhomogeneous synchronous coupling and verify these conditions for linear quadratic problems. Numerical experiments on linear quadratic models and the optimal consumption-investment problems in an incomplete market factor model illustrate policy improvement, convergence toward optimal policies, and the effect of decaying exploration noise.
tldr: The paper develops a continuous policy-value iteration method for infinite-horizon stochastic control problems using Langevin-type policy dynamics and simultaneous value updates.
motivation: The authors aim to avoid solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman PDE at each policy iteration while retaining policy improvement and convergence guarantees for stochastic control.
method: They couple policy updates via Langevin dynamics driven by an inhomogeneous Hamiltonian gradient with value-function updates, and prove exponential contraction in Wasserstein-2 distance under Lipschitz conditions via inhomogeneous synchronous coupling.
result: The framework establishes policy improvement and convergence for linear-quadratic problems and optimal consumption-investment models, with numerical experiments showing convergence and effects of decaying exploration noise.
conclusion: The proposed continuous policy-value iteration provides a theoretical and computational framework for stochastic control, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Statistical Guarantees For Covariance Estimation With Adversarial Corruption Under Constraints
authors: Samuel Ozminkowski, Hongmei Jiang, Matey Neykov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain a near-minimax rate on covariance estimation of adversarially corrupted Gaussian data in Frobenius norm when the covariance estimation is assumed to lie in a star-shaped set [MATH]. Assuming a known upper bound of [MATH] on the fraction of the [MATH] observations of data [MATH] are arbitrarily corrupted by an omniscient adversary, we obtain the near-minimax rate (up to constants) of \left(\varepsilon^2 \vee \delta^{\star2} \right)\wedge d^2 \lesssim \inf_{\hat\Sigma} \sup_{\Sigma \in K} \sup_{} \| \hat\Sigma((X)) - \Sigma \|_F^2 \lesssim \left(\varepsilon^2\log^2(1/\varepsilon) \vee \delta^{\star2} \right)\wedge d^2 where [MATH] is the diameter of the set [MATH], [MATH], and \delta^*=\sup\left\{ \delta\geq 0: {\Upsilon^2} \delta^2\leq \log _K^{}(\delta,c) \right\} for an arbitrary large constant [MATH] and the local metric entropy of [MATH], [MATH]. We believe this is the first such general result on structured robust covariance estimation in the Frobenius norm.
tldr: The paper establishes near-minimax rates for covariance estimation of adversarially corrupted Gaussian data under structural constraints in Frobenius norm.
motivation: Robust covariance estimation is important when data may be arbitrarily corrupted, but general structured minimax guarantees were lacking.
method: The authors analyze a star-shaped constraint set for the covariance, assume a known bound on the corrupted fraction, and derive upper and lower bounds using local metric entropy and the diameter of the set.
result: They obtain a near-minimax rate $\left(\varepsilon^2 \vee \delta^{\star2} \right)\wedge d^2 \lesssim \inf_{\hat\Sigma} \sup_{\Sigma \in K} \| \hat\Sigma - \Sigma \|_F^2 \lesssim \left(\varepsilon^2\log^2(1/\varepsilon) \vee \delta^{\star2} \right)\wedge d^2$, claimed as the first general structured robust covariance estimation result in Frobenius norm.
conclusion: The work provides statistical guarantees for robust covariance estimation under adversarial corruption and constrained parameter sets, but it is outside the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems research directions.

title: The Milnor Fiber As A Local Conley Index
authors: Nivaldo Grulha Jean-Paul Brasselet
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a holomorphic germ with an isolated critical point at the origin, and let [MATH] be the negative gradient flow of [MATH] with respect to a Riemannian metric. We show that the origin is an isolated invariant set of [MATH] and that its Conley index is the suspension of the Milnor fiber, \[ h(\varphi_f,\{0\})\;\simeq\;\Sigma F_f\;\simeq\;\bigvee_{\mu(f)}S^n , \] so that [MATH]: the Milnor number is the rank of the homological Conley index of the flow in degree [MATH]. The proof uses continuation to a holomorphic morsification of [MATH]. Since [MATH] is a first integral of the flow, after a rotation of the target through an angle avoiding finitely many values there are no connecting orbits between the [MATH] nondegenerate rest points that result, and the sum property of the Conley index applies. McCord's theorem then recovers the Poincar\'e--Hopf index of [MATH].
tldr: The paper identifies the local Conley index of the negative gradient flow of a holomorphic germ with isolated singularity as the suspension of the Milnor fiber, recovering the Milnor number as the rank of the homological Conley index.
motivation: The work connects dynamical systems invariants (Conley index) with singularity theory invariants (Milnor fiber, Milnor number) for holomorphic germs, providing a topological interpretation of the local flow near a critical point.
method: The authors use continuation to a holomorphic morsification and a rotation of the target to avoid connecting orbits, then apply the sum property of the Conley index and McCord's theorem.
result: They show that the origin is an isolated invariant set and its Conley index is homotopy equivalent to the suspension of the Milnor fiber, i.e., a wedge of μ(f) copies of S^n, so the Milnor number equals the rank of the homological Conley index in degree n.
conclusion: This establishes a direct link between the Conley index of the gradient flow and classical singularity invariants, and recovers the Poincaré–Hopf index via McCord's theorem.

title: Morse-Smale Dynamics In Discrete Huygens Networks
authors: Jorge Buescu, Emma D'aniello, Henrique M. Oliveira
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study discrete networks of [MATH] identical phase oscillators with positive reciprocal weights and smooth odd periodic interactions, motivated by discrete models of Huygens synchronisation. The interaction laws define an intrinsic potential, and removing the common phase gives a gradient map on the [MATH]-torus. A weighted graph Laplacian yields explicit step sizes for strict Lyapunov decrease and global invertibility. Our main result is a Morse--Smale criterion for maps [MATH]: if [MATH] is symmetric, nonsingular and weakly diagonally dominant, the map is Morse--Smale for [MATH], and this interval is optimal. The proof combines invariant coordinate slabs with a maximum principle for the adjoint variational equation. The criterion applies to unit-weight paths of any length and to the three-leaf star, and a weighted version covers paths with discretely concave weights. By structural stability, it extends to every graph containing a spanning path with sufficiently weak additional links. Conversely, we construct infinitely many trees with Morse potentials and an almost-global sink, whose maps nevertheless have non-transverse heteroclinic intersections.
tldr: The paper studies discrete networks of phase oscillators motivated by Huygens synchronisation and establishes a Morse-Smale criterion for the associated gradient maps on the torus using graph Laplacian techniques.
motivation: Discrete models of Huygens synchronisation are of interest in dynamical systems and network synchronization, but their global dynamical properties, such as Morse-Smale structure, are not fully understood.
method: The interaction laws yield an intrinsic potential and a gradient map on the N-torus; a weighted graph Laplacian provides explicit step sizes for Lyapunov decrease. The proof uses invariant coordinate slabs and a maximum principle for the adjoint variational equation.
result: For symmetric, nonsingular, weakly diagonally dominant maps, the map is Morse-Smale on an optimal interval of coupling strengths. This applies to unit-weight paths and the three-leaf star, and extensions cover discretely concave weights and graphs containing a spanning path. Counterexamples show trees with Morse potentials and an almost-global sink can have non-transverse heteroclinic intersections.
conclusion: The criterion gives a sharp condition for Morse-Smale dynamics in these Huygens networks and extends via structural stability, while also revealing limits through explicit counterexamples.

title: Vanishing Moment Dilations And Applications To Balanced And Graph Frames
authors: Deguang Han, Shankhadeep Mondal, Kai Liu, Omar Nour
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a matrix [MATH] we examine finite frames [MATH] with vanishing [MATH]-moments and investigate their connections with the frame dilation property. We establish several equivalent characterizations for the existence of vanishing [MATH]moment dilations, including conditions involving dual frames, operator ranges, and linear independence properties associated with the matrix [MATH]. In particular, we show that every frame with redundancy [MATH] admits a dual frame with vanishing [MATH]-moments for some totally nonsingular matrix [MATH]. A key takeaway of this is that by invoking such a dual frame as the encoding frame, any frame with redundancy [MATH] (erasure robustness is not needed) allows perfect signal reconstructions for any number of [MATH]-erasures ([MATH]) which only involves inverting a matrix of small size ([MATH]) instead of inverting the subframe operator which is a matrix of large size ([MATH]). A special case of this type of frames are [MATH]-th vanishing moment frames which have natural connections with graph frames. We characterize the existence of dual frames with [MATH] vanishing moments through polynomial cancellation identities and operator theoretical conditions. We further discuss some applications to problems in erasure recovery and graph frames. These results provide a unified framework linking vanishing moment conditions, dual frame theory, dilation theory, and graph theoretic constructions of frames.
tldr: The paper studies finite frames with vanishing M-moments and their connection to frame dilation, providing dual-frame constructions that enable efficient erasure recovery and linking to graph frames.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize when a frame admits a vanishing-moment dilation and to exploit dual frames with vanishing moments for perfect signal reconstruction under erasures without requiring erasure robustness.
method: They use matrix and operator-theoretic techniques, including dual frames, operator ranges, linear independence conditions, and polynomial cancellation identities, to establish equivalent characterizations.
result: Every frame with redundancy greater than the number of vanishing moments admits a dual frame with vanishing moments for some totally nonsingular matrix, allowing perfect reconstruction of any number of M-erasures by inverting only a small matrix.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework connecting vanishing moment conditions, dual frame theory, dilation theory, and graph-theoretic frame constructions, with applications to erasure recovery and graph frames.

title: Numerical Neural Operator: Connection Between Numerical Analysis And The Operator Learning And Building Discretized Neural Operators From Finite Element Methods
authors: Zecheng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operator learning aims to learn mappings between function spaces and has been widely used for PDE-related problems. This raises two fundamental questions. First, is there a connection between standard numerical methods and neural operators, given that both are designed to approximate PDE solution operators? Second, when a neural operator is trained on numerically generated data, does it approximate the underlying infinite dimension operator, the training data themselves, or the discretized numerical scheme used to generate them? A key hypothesis in the paper is that the trained neural operator may mimic the discretized numerical schemes that generate the training data. The hypothesis has been partially and preliminary verified by the linear approximation principle proposed in Chen Chen 1995 paper and the following scaling law papers. However, neural operator approximation from the perspective of numerical discretization remains unexplored. In this work, we consider a class of PDEs and derive neural operator architectures from the numerical schemes. Firstly, the numerical basis functions, such as finite element basis functions, can be approximated or directly constructed by learnable neural networks. Then the finite difference schemes for temporal discretization can be unrolled into iterative neural architectures that generate the coefficients of the basis of the resulting neural operator. By leveraging numerical analysis, we establish convergence error estimates for these numerically derived neural operators. Notably, the network size depends polynomial on the approximation error in [MATH], improving the nested exponential dependence derived in the general neural operator approximation and aligning with the numerical observations. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate reduced errors and improved parameter efficiency.
tldr: The paper derives neural operator architectures from numerical discretization schemes and proves convergence error estimates with improved polynomial network size scaling.
motivation: It investigates whether trained neural operators approximate the underlying infinite-dimensional operator, training data, or the discretized numerical scheme, and seeks to connect numerical analysis with operator learning.
method: The authors construct neural operators from finite element basis functions and finite difference temporal discretization, unrolling numerical schemes into iterative neural architectures and using numerical analysis to derive error estimates.
result: They establish convergence error estimates for the numerically derived neural operators, showing polynomial dependence of network size on approximation error, and numerical experiments demonstrate reduced errors and improved parameter efficiency.
conclusion: The work bridges numerical analysis and neural operator learning by embedding numerical schemes into neural architectures, potentially guiding more efficient and interpretable operator learning for PDEs.

title: Certified Corruption Budgets: Anytime-Valid Leaderboard Claims Under Adaptive Rigging
authors: Xiaoming Huo Hamed Khosravi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public leaderboards for AI models are read continuously, and attackers can see every published standing. Vote rigging, selective disclosure of private variants, and benchmark contamination can each move a ranking. Existing guarantees assume genuine records or bound the corruption per step, which an attacker who corrupts in bursts evades. We introduce the certified corruption budget, a tolerance [MATH] computed after [MATH] records and published with each pairwise claim. With probability at least [MATH], simultaneously at all times, the claim is correct or more than [MATH] records were corrupted. It holds against attackers who watch every certificate, with no bound on their budget. Forged records and records altered once seen require different certificates: the certificate for forgeries fails, with probability approaching one, against an attacker who flips votes it has seen, while one that charges roughly twice as much per record remains valid, with constant bets even against attackers who see the future, and no smaller charge is valid at every level. The certified budget grows nearly as fast as any valid method allows: with a win fraction [MATH], each new record adds close to [MATH] to the number of forged records the claim can withstand ([MATH] flipped). Publishing the best of [MATH] private variants costs only an amount growing like [MATH]. In replays on 1.8 million Chatbot Arena votes, a few hundred rigged votes make standard confidence intervals certify false orderings, while ours stays valid. On real votes, our certificate shows that clearly separated models withstand about 2,000 forged votes.
tldr: The paper introduces certified corruption budgets for leaderboard claims, providing anytime-valid certificates that remain correct unless many records are corrupted under adaptive rigging.
motivation: Public AI leaderboards are continuously read and vulnerable to vote rigging, selective disclosure, and benchmark contamination, while existing guarantees either assume genuine records or bound corruption per step and fail against bursty attackers.
method: It defines a certified corruption budget computed after n records and published with each pairwise claim, using separate certificates for forged versus altered records and deriving near-optimal growth rates for the budget.
result: The certificate fails against an attacker who flips already-seen votes but a roughly twice-as-costly version remains valid; in replays on 1.8 million Chatbot Arena votes, a few hundred rigged votes break standard confidence intervals while the new certificate stays valid, with clear model separations tolerating about 2,000 forged votes.
conclusion: The framework provides anytime-valid, adaptive-robust leaderboard claims with certified tolerance to corruption, offering a statistically principled alternative to standard confidence intervals.

title: MRCert: Towards Post-deployment Patch Robustness Certification For Adversarially Patched Samples Via Type-specific Masking
authors: Qilin Zhou, Zhengyuan Wei, Haipeng Wang, Zhuo Wang, Shuo Liu, W. K. Chan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In post-deployment time, inputs to deep learning models may or may not be adversarially patched. Patch robustness certification on such inputs within a patch bound can verify their label benignity and should retain high prediction accuracy. However, existing smoothing-based and masking-based recovery defenders cannot achieve both simultaneously: they degrade the prediction accuracy much and cannot verify the benignity of the returned label of an adversarially patched input, respectively. We propose MRCert, the first masking-based certified recovery defender that shows the feasibility of achieving both. Unlike all existing works to apply a common condition across both types of input (benign and adversarially patched samples) for certification, MRCert infers type-specific necessary properties of deep learning models for both types in post-deployment time and formally relates them to verify the label benignity through a novel type-oriented design of label recovery and certification function pair. Without incurring the degradation in clean accuracy caused by smoothing, experimental results confirm that MRCert achieves 35.1\% adversarial certified accuracy on ImageNet at patch size 16 pixels, whereas the SOTA PatchCURE fails completely.
tldr: MRCert introduces a type-specific masking-based certified recovery defender that achieves both high clean accuracy and adversarial patch robustness certification for deep learning models.
motivation: Existing smoothing-based and masking-based recovery defenders cannot simultaneously maintain high prediction accuracy and verify the benignity of labels for adversarially patched inputs.
method: MRCert infers type-specific necessary properties of deep learning models for benign and adversarially patched samples, and uses a novel type-oriented design of a label recovery and certification function pair.
result: On ImageNet at patch size 16 pixels, MRCert achieves 35.1% adversarial certified accuracy, whereas the state-of-the-art PatchCURE fails completely, without degrading clean accuracy.
conclusion: MRCert demonstrates the feasibility of achieving both high accuracy and certified robustness against adversarial patches in post-deployment settings.

title: Safe At One Loop, Risky At Another: Aligning Safety Across Recurrent Depths In Looped Language Models
authors: Yi Wang, Xiuyuan Qi, Dongqi Han, Dongsheng Li, Wenjie Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Looped Language Models (LoopLMs) provide a parameter efficient approach to scaling model capabilities through repeated use of shared parameters across recurrent steps. Since each recurrent depth can be read out independently, a single LoopLM exposes a broader output space across inference depths, raising an important question: whether safety is preserved throughout recurrent computation. Prior evaluations suggest that deeper recurrence can improve safety on harmful queries, but robustness under jailbreak attacks remains unclear. We therefore conduct a comprehensive safety evaluation of LoopLMs under jailbreak attacks targeting different recurrent depths. We find that attack success can increase at deeper inference depths, the same query can elicit different safety behaviors across depths, and attacks constructed against one depth can transfer to others. Moreover, SFT and preference alignment do not eliminate these safety gaps, motivating an alignment method designed for LoopLMs. We introduce SafeBridge, which combines lightweight depth specific control of shared recurrent layers, selective state bridging, and joint safety supervision across recurrent depths. Across model scales, multiple attack methods, and safety benchmarks, SafeBridge substantially reduces attack success for both matched-depth and cross-depth attacks. It also improves general utility over the vanilla models while maintaining comparable over-refusal behavior. Our results show that the safety of a LoopLM cannot be inferred from a single recurrent depth, motivating safety alignment across recurrent computation. Our code and model checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.
tldr: Evaluates safety across recurrent depths in looped language models under jailbreak attacks and proposes SafeBridge, a depth-aware alignment method.
motivation: Looped language models reuse shared parameters across recurrent steps, exposing multiple inference depths, but it is unclear whether safety is preserved across these depths under adversarial attacks.
method: The authors conduct a comprehensive safety evaluation of LoopLMs under jailbreak attacks targeting different recurrent depths and introduce SafeBridge, which combines depth-specific control, selective state bridging, and joint safety supervision across recurrent depths.
result: Attack success can increase at deeper inference depths, safety behaviors vary across depths, and attacks transfer across depths; SafeBridge reduces attack success for both matched-depth and cross-depth attacks while improving utility with comparable over-refusal.
conclusion: The safety of a LoopLM cannot be inferred from a single recurrent depth, motivating safety alignment across recurrent computation.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Public Project Redistribution Without Bounded Precision: A Complex-Analytic Proof
authors: Mingyu Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study worst-case VCG redistribution mechanism design for the public project problem, where n agents decide whether to build a non-excludable public project and the designer chooses a Groves term that returns as much of the VCG payment as possible without running a deficit. The objective is the worst-case efficiency ratio, the worst-case ratio between the agents' total utility and the first-best total utility. Prior work showed that this ratio can approach 1 as n grows only under a bounded precision assumption, that all types are rational numbers with a common bounded denominator. The assumption is stronger than it looks: it confines the difficult profiles to those in which all but a bounded number of agents report zero, and an agent who reports zero knows the total exactly. Without it, the best known guarantee tends to 1/2. We remove the assumption. We construct a deterministic, anonymous, strategy-proof, and non-deficit mechanism for arbitrary real types in [0,1] whose worst-case efficiency ratio is 1-O(1/log log n). The construction estimates the shortfall of the reported total below the project cost by filling in each agent's missing report with a resampled one, then estimates the error of that estimate, then the error of the error, and so on. After m rounds the aggregate error is at most 1/Hm mean reports, where Hm is the mth harmonic number. The proof of this bound is the heart of the paper and, unusually for a result about payments, uses complex analysis: a trigonometric representation of the shortfall function together with the Poisson-Jensen inequality for bounded analytic functions in the upper half plane.
tldr: The paper removes a bounded-precision assumption in worst-case VCG redistribution mechanism design for the public project problem and constructs an asymptotically optimal mechanism using complex analysis.
motivation: Prior work could approach full efficiency only under a bounded precision assumption on agent types, which implicitly restricted the hard instances; the authors aim to remove this assumption and handle arbitrary real types.
method: They design a deterministic, anonymous, strategy-proof, non-deficit mechanism that iteratively resamples missing reports and bounds the aggregate error using a trigonometric representation and the Poisson-Jensen inequality for bounded analytic functions.
result: The mechanism achieves a worst-case efficiency ratio of 1 - O(1/log log n) for arbitrary real types in [0,1], improving on the previous best guarantee of 1/2 without the bounded precision assumption.
conclusion: The bounded precision assumption is unnecessary for asymptotically optimal public project redistribution, and the complex-analytic proof establishes a strong guarantee for the worst-case efficiency ratio.

title: False Claims, Credible Images: A Red-Teaming Benchmark For Commercial Image Generators
authors: Zeyu Ye, Yanchun Li, Sibei He, Meng Xie, Hangtao Zhang, Xianlong Wang, Li Zeng, Jiahao Chen, Yichen Wang, Junhui Wang, Ziqi Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Image-generation models can now produce text-rich, natural-looking visual artifacts that are hard to distinguish from real-world evidence, such as news reports and textbook pages. Yet, the same capability introduces a new risk: these models can just as easily fabricate visual misinformation. Even commercial models (e.g., GPT-Image-2) readily produce it. Curiously, we find that these models can recognize a claim as false when asked, yet still render that very claim as credible visual evidence. This discrepancy points to a blind spot in current alignment: safeguards judge what an image shows, not what it asserts; however, existing red-teaming benchmarks target conventional harmful content, such as violent or explicit imagery, and say little about where the alignment boundaries lie for visual misinformation, especially in commercial models. To fill this gap, we introduce EpiReal-Bench, the first systematic benchmark for evaluating visual misinformation risks in commercial image generators, comprising 10k false-claim prompts and 10k corresponding generated images that span 10 real-world claim categories and 10 credible visual formats. We further introduce EpiReal-Attack, a skill-guided black-box optimization framework that uses Pareto-based selection and multimodal feedback to identify commands that bypass alignment safeguards while preserving visual realism, textual legibility, and semantic fidelity. Experiments on four commercial models reveal that more than 70% of false-claim prompts elicit images that faithfully depict the corresponding misinformation, and EpiReal-Attack pushes this rate to 95%. Most worryingly, these models are only a click away, and their outputs are cheap to spread yet hard to disbelieve, leaving this dimension of alignment largely unguarded.
tldr: The paper introduces EpiReal-Bench and EpiReal-Attack to benchmark and exploit visual misinformation risks in commercial image generators.
motivation: Commercial image generators can fabricate credible visual misinformation, yet existing red-teaming benchmarks focus on conventional harmful content without addressing false claims rendered as credible evidence.
method: The authors build a benchmark of 10k false-claim prompts and corresponding generated images across 10 claim categories and 10 visual formats, and develop a skill-guided black-box optimization framework using Pareto-based selection and multimodal feedback to bypass alignment safeguards.
result: Experiments on four commercial models show over 70% of false-claim prompts produce faithful misinformation images, and EpiReal-Attack raises this to 95% while preserving realism, legibility, and semantic fidelity.
conclusion: Visual misinformation in commercial image generators remains largely unguarded, creating a cheap and hard-to-disbelieve threat that current alignment safeguards do not address.

title: Characterizing Statistical Separability In Tp-criv For Probabilistic Ai Models
authors: Teruki Sano, Minoru Kuribayashi, Masao Sakai, Shuji Isobe, Eisuke Koizumi, Zhang Zhang, Satoru Matsumoto
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Third-party challenge-response identity verification (TP-CRIV) enables an independent verifier to assess whether a claimant possesses a model identical to a remotely deployed model without directly accessing the reference model. However, for probabilistic AI models, repeated executions of the same query may produce different outputs and therefore different verification observations. This raises the question of how such stochastic evidence should be accumulated and how much evidence is required for reliable verification. In this work, we characterize statistical separability in TP-CRIV of probabilistic AI models. Specifically, we relate challenge-wise behavior of matching and non-matching provers to verification-level separability. The characterization explicitly describes how the numbers of independent challenges and repeated responses affect detection performance and enables the verification budget required for a target AUC to be estimated. We instantiate the proposed characterization for LLMs using open-ended challenges. The experiments demonstrate matching-non-matching separation, close agreement between theoretical and empirical AUCs, and consistent estimates of the minimum verification budgets. These results provide a statistical basis for relating probabilistic model behavior to verification-level separability and the evidence required for third-party verification.
tldr: This paper characterizes statistical separability in third-party challenge-response identity verification (TP-CRIV) for probabilistic AI models, relating challenge-wise behavior to verification-level detection performance and estimating required verification budgets.
motivation: For probabilistic AI models, repeated queries produce stochastic outputs, raising the question of how to accumulate evidence and how many challenges are needed for reliable third-party verification.
method: The authors derive a statistical characterization linking matching and non-matching prover behavior at the challenge level to verification-level separability, explicitly accounting for independent challenges and repeated responses, and instantiate it for LLMs with open-ended challenges.
result: Experiments demonstrate matching-non-matching separation, close agreement between theoretical and empirical AUCs, and consistent estimates of minimum verification budgets for target AUCs.
conclusion: The work provides a statistical basis for relating probabilistic model behavior to verification-level separability and evidence requirements in third-party verification, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory and its subfields.

title: Soft Voting For Policy-Aware Private Data Synthesis
authors: Yingge Hu, Gautham Ramesh Babu, Mostafa Milani
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blowfish privacy relaxes differential privacy (DP) by protecting only the attribute-value substitutions a data owner specifies as edges of a policy graph. A sparser policy can reduce the noise required by a mechanism, but only when the released statistic changes less across protected substitutions than across arbitrary DP neighbors. We study this question for evolutionary, nearest-neighbor DP synthesizers such as Private Evolution (PE) and its tabular instantiation Tab-PE, which score private records against a candidate population and release a noisy vote histogram. Their hard vote is constant inside each candidate's decision region and jumps at its boundary. Its policy-specific sensitivity therefore equals the full worst-case value whenever at least one protected substitution crosses a boundary, regardless of how short that substitution is. Because every round we examined contained such a substitution, the policy graph gave no reduction in noise. We propose BF-Soft, a temperature-smoothed soft vote whose response changes gradually with distance. Its sensitivity has a tight closed-form bound in the policy graph's reach and the temperature, independent of the number of candidates, and the bound can be computed once before synthesis. It also predicts from the policy alone when policy-aware smoothing cannot substantially reduce noise: protecting a flat categorical or binary attribute drives the reach to its maximum. On real and synthetic datasets under narrow numeric policies, BF-Soft reduces error relative to hard voting at strong privacy budgets, while the advantage reverses at weaker budgets. A public-data pilot predicts when soft voting is beneficial without spending private budget.
tldr: The paper proposes BF-Soft, a temperature-smoothed soft voting mechanism for policy-aware private data synthesis under Blowfish privacy, improving over hard voting in some privacy regimes but not directly relevant to quantum information research.
motivation: Blowfish privacy can reduce noise when protected substitutions are less sensitive than arbitrary differential privacy neighbors, but hard-vote synthesizers like Private Evolution and Tab-PE often achieve no reduction because their decision boundaries create worst-case sensitivity.
method: The authors introduce BF-Soft, a temperature-smoothed soft vote whose sensitivity has a closed-form bound depending on the policy graph's reach and temperature, and they predict from the policy alone when smoothing cannot substantially reduce noise.
result: On real and synthetic datasets under narrow numeric policies, BF-Soft reduces error relative to hard voting at strong privacy budgets, while the advantage reverses at weaker budgets; a public-data pilot predicts benefit without spending private budget.
conclusion: Policy-aware soft voting can improve private synthesis in certain regimes, but its benefits are limited by the policy graph structure, and the work lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Refinement As A Service: Algorithmic Predictor Refinement
authors: Hanrui Zhang Wei Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prediction aggregation aims to combine information from multiple predictors into a more informative one. We study this question in the setting of calibrated predictors, where each prediction must equal the conditional expectation of the quantity being predicted given the predictor's signal. Given several calibrated input predictors and the feature distribution, but not the underlying Bayes probabilities, we ask when one can construct refined calibrated predictors that preserve the information in the original predictors and cannot be further refined using the available information. We formulate calibrated predictors as signaling schemes and define refinement through feature-independent garblings: a predictor refines another if its signal can simulate the other's signal. Constructibility is characterized through observable linear information: each signal corresponds to a vector over the feature space, and a new signal is constructible exactly when its vector lies in the linear span of the input signal vectors. Under this formulation, we establish a sharp algorithmic picture. For deterministic output predictors, bilateral refinement admits a polynomial-time algorithm based on a bipartite graph between the two input signal partitions, while refinement with an arbitrary number of input predictors is [MATH]-hard. In contrast, when randomized output predictors are allowed, we give a polynomial-time algorithm for any number of input predictors by decomposing constructible signal vectors into extreme rays of the associated polyhedral cone.
tldr: The paper studies algorithmic refinement of calibrated predictors, framing them as signaling schemes and characterizing constructibility via the linear span of signal vectors.
motivation: Prediction aggregation aims to combine multiple calibrated predictors into a more informative calibrated predictor without access to the underlying Bayes probabilities.
method: Predictors are modeled as signaling schemes, refinement is defined through feature-independent garblings, and constructibility is characterized by observable linear information where each signal corresponds to a vector over the feature space.
result: For deterministic output predictors, bilateral refinement admits a polynomial-time bipartite-graph algorithm while refinement with an arbitrary number of predictors is NP-hard; for randomized predictors, a polynomial-time algorithm decomposes constructible signal vectors into extreme rays of a polyhedral cone.
conclusion: The work provides a sharp algorithmic picture of predictor refinement, distinguishing deterministic and randomized settings via a linear-algebraic characterization.

title: Marc: Multi-Bit Watermarking For Autoregressive Audio Generation Against Codec Attacks
authors: Liaoran Xu, Weizhi Liu, Zhaoxia Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generated audio is now used in a range of applications, creating a need to verify its origin after distribution and signal processing. This task is particularly challenging for autoregressive audio generation because codec processing can alter the token sequence recovered from the waveform. Such changes reduce the reliability of watermark detection and payload decoding. Existing methods construct token groups using either intrinsic token representations or substitution patterns caused by transformations. As a result, intrinsic token relationships and codec induced substitutions are modeled separately. In addition, most methods support only zero bit detection. They can determine whether a watermark is present but cannot distinguish individual generated outputs. We propose , a multi-bit generative watermarking method for autoregressive audio generation. MARC integrates intrinsic token representations with confusion patterns obtained through retokenization and multiple codecs, forming a codec-aware token-cluster space. Within this space, payload-driven cluster scheduling is used to embed a multi-bit watermark, while detection and payload decoding are performed on retokenized observations. Experiments on speech, dialogue, and music generation show that MARC achieves an average of 97.3\% bit extraction accuracy on unmodified watermarked audio and the watermark can still be extracted under diverse codec attacks. MARC also demonstrates robustness to overwriting attacks.
tldr: MARC is a multi-bit watermarking method for autoregressive audio generation that remains extractable under codec and overwriting attacks.
motivation: Generated audio needs origin verification, but existing watermarking for autoregressive models struggles because codec processing alters token sequences and most methods support only zero-bit detection.
method: MARC integrates intrinsic token representations with confusion patterns from retokenization and multiple codecs into a codec-aware token-cluster space, then uses payload-driven cluster scheduling to embed a multi-bit watermark and decode from retokenized observations.
result: Experiments on speech, dialogue, and music generation show 97.3% average bit extraction accuracy on unmodified watermarked audio, with robust extraction under diverse codec attacks and overwriting attacks.
conclusion: MARC enables reliable multi-bit watermarking for autoregressive audio generation despite codec-induced token changes, improving robustness and payload capacity over zero-bit approaches.

title: Antichains For Concurrent Parameterized Games
authors: Nathalie Bertrand (universit\'e de Rennes, Inria, CNRS, IRISA, Rennes, France), Patricia Bouyer (LMF, CNRS,ENS Paris-Saclay, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, Gif-Sur-Yvette, France), Ga\"etan Staquet
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Concurrent parameterized games involve a fixed yet arbitrary number of players. They are described by finite arenas in which the edges are labeled with languages that describe the possible move combinations leading from one vertex to another (n players yield a word of length n). Previous work showed that, when edge labels are regular languages, one can decide whether a distinguished player, called Eve, has a strategy to ensure a reachability objective, against any strategy profile of her arbitrarily many opponents. This decision problem is known to be PSPACE-complete. A basic ingredient in the PSPACE-membership proof is the reduction to the exponential-size knowledge game, a 2-player game that reflects the knowledge Eve has on the number of opponents. In this paper, we provide a symbolic approach, based on antichains, to compute Eve's winning region in the knowledge game. In words, it gives the minimal knowledge Eve needs at every vertex to win the concurrent parameterized reachability game. More precisely, we propose two fixed-point algorithms that compute, as an antichain, the maximal elements of the winning region for Eve in the knowledge game. We implemented these two algorithms in C++, as well as the one initially proposed, and report on their relative performances on various benchmarks.
tldr: The paper develops antichain-based fixed-point algorithms to compute Eve's winning region in the knowledge game arising from concurrent parameterized reachability games.
motivation: Concurrent parameterized games model systems with an arbitrary number of players, and deciding reachability objectives is PSPACE-complete via a reduction to an exponential-size knowledge game. A symbolic approach could improve practical performance.
method: The authors propose two fixed-point algorithms that compute, as an antichain, the maximal elements of Eve's winning region in the knowledge game, and implement them in C++ alongside the previously known algorithm.
result: The algorithms are implemented and benchmarked against the original algorithm, with relative performance reported on various benchmarks.
conclusion: Antichain-based symbolic computation offers an alternative method for solving concurrent parameterized reachability games, with empirical comparison to prior work.

title: Uniformity Theory Of Weighted Composites
authors: Mohammadjavad Javadi Marcelo Epstein
abstract: ArXiv:2610.11157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By including spatially varying volume fractions of the constituents, composites are obtained that are akin to functionally graded media. An extension of the mathematical apparatus of double groupoids is proposed to incorporate these materials with the aim of eventually classifying defects of misalignment and their time evolution.
tldr: The paper extends double groupoid methods to model spatially varying composites and classify misalignment defects.
motivation: Composites with spatially varying volume fractions behave like functionally graded media but require suitable mathematical tools for defect classification and evolution.
method: An extension of the mathematical apparatus of double groupoids is proposed to incorporate weighted composites.
result: The framework enables representation of functionally graded media and provides a route to classifying defects of misalignment and their time evolution.
conclusion: Double groupoid formalism offers a promising approach for uniformity theory of weighted composites and defect analysis.

title: Gain Of Entrainment In Ribosome Flow Models With Nonlinear Steric Hindrance: Global Rigidity And Dimension-Induced Gai
authors: Hui Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.10602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ribosome flow model (RFM) is a nonlinear compartmental model for unidirectional transport along an mRNA chain. We study a generalized RFM in which the classical linear free-space factor is replaced by a monotone nonlinear steric-hindrance response. After recalling the global equilibrium and periodic entrainment properties needed for the analysis, we derive an exact weighted edge-dissipation identity for the gain of entrainment (GOE). This yields a global no-GOE criterion formulated through the curvature of the nonlinear hindrance law. In particular, the quadratic hindrance model admits no positive GOE in any dimension and for arbitrary periodic forcing amplitudes, with equality only when all rates share a common multiplicative modulation. In one dimension, we obtain a sharp convexity-based classification and construct positive-GOE examples when the relevant convexity fails. In higher dimensions, the second variation is governed by a symmetric Jacobi matrix whose diagonal terms encode local curvature and whose off-diagonal entries represent nearest-neighbor transport coupling. This leads to an exact Riccati criterion, a dimension-uniform condition for heterogeneous chains, and a closed-form critical dimension in the homogeneous case. We also exhibit a nonlinear hindrance for which low-dimensional chains have no positive second-order GOE, while a higher-dimensional chain admits a realizable positive GOE. These results reveal a dimension-induced gain mechanism that is absent from the classical RFM.
tldr: The paper studies gain of entrainment in a generalized ribosome flow model with nonlinear steric hindrance, deriving global and dimension-dependent criteria for positive entrainment gain.
motivation: Ribosome flow models describe unidirectional transport along mRNA, and understanding periodic entrainment and its gain is important for nonlinear compartmental dynamics, but the work is purely classical and biological.
method: The authors derive an exact weighted edge-dissipation identity, a global no-GOE criterion via curvature of the hindrance law, and in higher dimensions analyze the second variation using a Jacobi matrix, leading to a Riccati criterion and a critical dimension.
